claim: Drosophila central neurons arise from neuroblasts that generate neurons in a pair-wise fashion, with the two daughters providing the basis for distinct A and B hemilineage groups.
source: Drosophila central neurons arise from neuroblasts that generate neurons in a pair-wise fashion, with the two daughters providing the basis for distinct A and B hemilineage groups.
evidence: This is a direct statement from the abstract describing the developmental origin of Drosophila neurons.

claim: 33 postembryonically-born hemilineages contribute over 90% of the neurons in each thoracic hemisegment.
source: 33 postembryonically-born hemilineages contribute over 90% of the neurons in each thoracic hemisegment.
evidence: This is a quantitative statement about the contribution of hemilineages to thoracic neurons.

claim: The simplest hemilineages contained local interneurons and their activation caused tonic or phasic leg movements lacking interlimb coordination.
source: The simplest hemilineages contained local interneurons and their activation caused tonic or phasic leg movements lacking interlimb coordination.
evidence: This describes experimental observations from activation studies.

claim: Hemilineages of similar projection cells drove intersegmentally coordinated behaviors such as walking.
source: The next level was hemilineages of similar projection cells that drove intersegmentally coordinated behaviors such as walking.
evidence: This describes behavioral outcomes from activation experiments.

claim: Activation of the highest level hemilineages elicited complex behaviors such as takeoff.
source: The highest level involved hemilineages whose activation elicited complex behaviors such as takeoff.
evidence: This describes experimental results from hemilineage activation.

claim: The Drosophila CNS has on the order of 100,000 neurons.
source: Even the small CNS of Drosophila has on the order of 100,000 neurons (Power, 1943; Chiang et al., 2011), each of which is capable of making connections with dozens of synaptic partners.
evidence: This is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: Each Drosophila neuron is capable of making connections with dozens of synaptic partners.
source: Even the small CNS of Drosophila has on the order of 100,000 neurons (Power, 1943; Chiang et al., 2011), each of which is capable of making connections with dozens of synaptic partners.
evidence: This is a general statement about neuronal connectivity based on established knowledge.

claim: In the vertebrate spinal cord, identified progenitor cells generate discrete pools of interneurons which have defined roles in producing functional circuits.
source: In the spinal cord, for example, identified progenitor cells generate discrete pools of interneurons, which in turn have defined roles in producing functional circuits (Grillner and Jessell, 2009).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to published work.

claim: The functional organization of the spinal cord in vertebrates is conserved from fish through mammals.
source: The functional organization of the spinal cord in vertebrates appears to be conserved, in that the progenitor cells and transcription factors that characterize different interneuron classes are conserved from fish through mammals (Lupo et al., 2006) despite the marked differences in modes of locomotion.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to published literature.

claim: The ventral nervous system (VNS) of insects is the site of sensorimotor patterning for complex behaviors such as walking, jumping, and flight.
source: Like the vertebrate spinal cord, the ventral nervous system (VNS) of insects is the site of sensorimotor patterning for complex behaviors such as walking, jumping, and flight.
evidence: This is based on established knowledge about insect neuroanatomy and function.

claim: In grasshoppers, NB 4-1 produces the cluster of midline spiking interneurons that receive exteroceptor input and shape the receptive fields of leg motoneurons.
source: In the grasshopper, for example, NB 4-1 has been shown to produce the cluster of midline spiking interneurons that receive exteroceptor input and shape the receptive fields of leg motoneurons (Shepherd and Laurent, 1992).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to published work.

claim: The unpaired medial NB in grasshoppers produces the pool of local, midline GABAergic neurons that respond to sound.
source: Similarly, the unpaired medial NB produces the pool of local, midline GABAergic neurons that respond to sound (Thompson and Siegler, 1991).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to published work.

claim: The insect VNS develops according to a conservative plan based on a segmental set of 30 paired and one unpaired NBs that has changed little through 350 million years of insect evolution.
source: The finding that specific stem cells generate pools of functionally similar interneurons has important evolutionary implications because the insect VNS develops according to a conservative plan based on a segmental set of 30 paired and one unpaired NBs that has changed little through the 350 million years of insect evolution (Thomas et al., 1984; Truman and Ball, 1998).
evidence: This is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: Each NB in insects is uniquely identifiable and characterized by its position in the array, its pattern of molecular expression, and the suite of early neurons that it produces.
source: Each NB is uniquely identifiable and characterized by its position in the array, its pattern of molecular expression (Broadus and Doe, 1995), and the suite of early neurons that it produces (Bossing et al., 1996; Schmid et al., 1999).
evidence: This is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: The number of thoracic neurons roughly doubled with the evolution of flight in insects.
source: Comparative studies between a basal, primitively flightless insect and flying insects showed that the number of thoracic neurons roughly doubled with the evolution of flight.
evidence: This is based on comparative studies described in the text.

claim: The increase in thoracic neurons with flight evolution came from extending the proliferative phase of existing NBs rather than adding new NBs.
source: This increase did not come from adding new NBs, but rather was correlated with a subset of the NBs making more neurons by extending their proliferative phase (Truman and Ball, 1998).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to published work.

claim: During the postembryonic phase in Drosophila, each NB divides repeatedly, with the smaller product of each division being a ganglion mother cell (GMC), which then terminally divides to produce two neurons.
source: During this postembryonic phase, each NB divides repeatedly, with the smaller product of each division being a ganglion mother cell (GMC), which then terminally divides to produce two neurons.
evidence: This describes the developmental process based on established knowledge.

claim: By the start of metamorphosis, each NB and its immature progeny form a discrete cell cluster from which one or two axon bundles project to specific regions in the larval neuropil.
source: By the start of metamorphosis each NB and its immature progeny form a discrete cell cluster from which one or two axon bundles project to specific regions in the larval neuropil (Truman et al., 2004).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to published work.

claim: Each axon bundle identifies the neurons of a hemilineage, a set of neuronal 'cousins' that includes either the 'A' (Notch-on) or 'B' (Notch-off) daughter from the GMC division.
source: Each axon bundle identifies the neurons of a hemilineage, a set of neuronal 'cousins' that includes either the 'A' (Notch-on) or 'B' (Notch-off) daughter from the GMC division (Truman et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to published work.

claim: In Drosophila, 25 of the 30 embryonic NBs in a hemisegment generate postembryonic lineage.
source: In Drosophila, 25 of the 30 embryonic NBs in a hemisegment generate postembryonic lineage.
evidence: This is a quantitative statement about NB development.

claim: Of the 50 possible hemilineages in Drosophila, 17 are removed by programmed cell death.
source: Of the 50 possible hemilineages, 17 are removed by programmed cell death so that a segmental unit of the adult thoracic CNS contains neurons from only 33 hemilineage-based pools.
evidence: This is a quantitative statement about hemilineage development.

claim: A segmental unit of the adult thoracic CNS contains neurons from 33 hemilineage-based pools.
source: Of the 50 possible hemilineages, 17 are removed by programmed cell death so that a segmental unit of the adult thoracic CNS contains neurons from only 33 hemilineage-based pools.
evidence: This is a quantitative statement about adult CNS composition.

claim: The 33 hemilineages account for 90–95% of the neurons in the adult thoracic CNS.
source: These account for 90–95% of the neurons in the adult thoracic CNS.
evidence: This is a quantitative statement about neuronal composition.

claim: Expression of many early transcription factors is restricted along hemilineage lines.
source: Expression of many early transcription factors is restricted along hemilineage lines (Lacin et al., 2014) and many of these transcription factors have homologs involved in fate determination in the vertebrate spinal cord (Thor and Thomas, 1997).
evidence: This is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: Many transcription factors expressed in Drosophila hemilineages have homologs involved in fate determination in the vertebrate spinal cord.
source: Expression of many early transcription factors is restricted along hemilineage lines (Lacin et al., 2014) and many of these transcription factors have homologs involved in fate determination in the vertebrate spinal cord (Thor and Thomas, 1997).
evidence: This is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: The homeodomain protein Dbx1 controls the difference between the V0 and V1 fates in the mouse spinal cord.
source: For example, the homeodomain protein Dbx1 controls the difference between the V0 and V1 fates in the mouse spinal cord (Pierani et al., 2001), while the Drosophila homolog, dbx, controls differentiation of particular VNS cell types through interactions with even-skipped and hb9 (Lacin et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to published work.

claim: The Drosophila homolog of Dbx1, dbx, controls differentiation of particular VNS cell types through interactions with even-skipped and hb9.
source: For example, the homeodomain protein Dbx1 controls the difference between the V0 and V1 fates in the mouse spinal cord (Pierani et al., 2001), while the Drosophila homolog, dbx, controls differentiation of particular VNS cell types through interactions with even-skipped and hb9 (Lacin et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to published work.

claim: Most hemilineages are composed of pools of similar interneurons.
source: We find that most hemilineages are composed of pools of similar interneurons, confirming that neuronal classes are indeed based on a hemilineage plan.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental observations in this study.

claim: Stimulation of interneurons in a hemilineage pool using dTRPA1 elicits a characteristic, often unique, behavioral response from each.
source: Stimulation of interneurons in a hemilineage pool using the temperature-sensitive cation channel dTRPA1 (Hamada et al., 2008) elicits a characteristic, often unique, behavioral response from each.
evidence: This describes experimental results from this study, with a citation for the dTRPA1 method.

claim: The complexity of the elicited behavior reflects the complexity of the hemilineage's projection pattern and the neuropil region to which it projects.
source: The complexity of the elicited behavior reflects the complexity of the hemilineage's projection pattern and the neuropil region to which it projects.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from correlating anatomical and behavioral data.

claim: Hemilineages provide a functional as well as an anatomical ground plan for the thoracic nervous system.
source: These findings suggest that the hemilineages provide a functional as well as an anatomical ground plan for the thoracic nervous system, and that thorax-mediated behaviors occur by combinations of simple movements elicited by relatively simple ventral hemilineages, which are then orchestrated by a hierarchy of increasingly complex dorsal hemilineages.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental findings.

claim: Thorax-mediated behaviors occur by combinations of simple movements elicited by relatively simple ventral hemilineages, which are then orchestrated by a hierarchy of increasingly complex dorsal hemilineages.
source: These findings suggest that the hemilineages provide a functional as well as an anatomical ground plan for the thoracic nervous system, and that thorax-mediated behaviors occur by combinations of simple movements elicited by relatively simple ventral hemilineages, which are then orchestrated by a hierarchy of increasingly complex dorsal hemilineages.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental findings.

claim: Hemilineages 0A, 4A, 16B and 17A are not addressed in this study.
source: Of the 33 major thoracic hemilineages, hemilineages 0A, 4A, 16B and 17A are not addressed in this study.
evidence: This is a direct statement about the scope of the study.

claim: The Rubin GAL4 collection is based on over 7000 cis-regulatory regions (CRMs).
source: Since each hemilineage can be identified in the larva based on cluster position and trajectory of its axon bundle (Truman et al., 2010), we screened the larval expression patterns of the Rubin GAL4 collection (Jenett et al., 2012) based on over 7000 cis-regulatory regions (CRMs; see Pfeiffer et al., 2008), for lines that drove expression in single hemilineages (Li et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: In the last instar larva, line R24B02-GAL4 drives expression in the cells of hemilineage 12A from the subesophageal through the A1 segments.
source: In the last instar larva, line R24B02-GAL4 drives expression in the cells of hemilineage 12A from the subesophageal through the A1 segments (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: The R24B02-GAL4 expression pattern wanes during metamorphosis and is replaced by a different set of cells in the adult CNS.
source: However, this expression pattern wanes during metamorphosis and is replaced by a different set of cells in the adult CNS (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: RU486 given to feeding larvae is effectively cleared from the animal during metamorphosis.
source: Feeding adults with RU486 reinduced GFP expression but only in the expected adult pattern and not in the 12A interneurons. Consequently, the RU486 given to feeding larvae is effectively cleared from the animal during metamorphosis (this study).
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from experimental observations in this study.

claim: A driver for nSynaptobrevin (R57C10-GAL4) drives expression in functioning primary neurons, but not in clusters of arrested immature secondary neurons.
source: We first confirmed that a driver for such a gene—R57C10-GAL4 that carries an 872-bp promoter fragment from the nSynaptobrevin gene (nSyb; Pfeiffer et al., 2008; Pfeiffer et al., 2012)—drives expression in the functioning primary neurons, but not in the clusters of arrested immature secondary neurons (Figure 3A, inset).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: nSyb-GAL80 suppresses expression in mature neurons, leaving only expression in arrested immature neurons.
source: When crossed into lines that contained a mixture of functioning larval neurons and clusters of arrested, postembryonic cells (Figure 3B), nSyb-GAL80 suppressed expression in the mature neurons, leaving only the expression in the arrested immature neurons (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figures 3B and 3C.

claim: The initial projections that hemilineage groups make in the larva prefigure their target regions in the adult CNS.
source: We find that the initial projections that these hemilineage groups make in the larva (Truman et al., 2004) prefigure their target regions in the adult CNS.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from anatomical observations, with a citation to prior work.

claim: Two motor hemilineages (15B and 24B) and fifteen interneuron hemilineages form the immature 'leg neuropil' of the larva and all make neurons exclusively for the adult leg neuropil.
source: Two motor hemilineages (15B and 24B) and fifteen interneuron hemilineages form the immature 'leg neuropil' of the larva (Truman et al., 2004) and all of these make neurons exclusively for the adult leg neuropil.
evidence: This is supported by anatomical observations and a citation to prior work.

claim: Hemilineage 23B is the only mature leg hemilineage that resides outside of the larval leg neuropil.
source: The only mature leg hemilineage that resides outside of the larval leg neuropil is hemilineage 23B whose mature neurons have dendrites in the most ventral regions of the leg neuropil where they overlap the leg afferents.
evidence: This is based on anatomical observations.

claim: Hemilineage 23B neurons may be excluded from the immature leg neuropil because their inputs do not grow into the CNS until metamorphosis is well underway.
source: They may be excluded from the immature leg neuropil because their inputs do not grow into the CNS until metamorphosis is well underway.
evidence: This is a speculative explanation for the observed anatomy.

claim: The neurons in many of the leg hemilineages constitute a relatively homogeneous group with arbors in restricted regions of the leg neuropil.
source: The neurons in many of the leg hemilineages constitute a relatively homogeneous group with arbors in restricted regions of the leg neuropil.
evidence: This is based on anatomical observations.

claim: The dendrites of 23B neurons and the neurons of the 9A group overlap the terminals of exteroceptors and proprioceptors, respectively.
source: On the sensory side, the dendrites of the above-mentioned 23B neurons and the neurons of the 9A group overlap the terminals of exteroceptors and proprioceptors, respectively (Harris, 2012) and are likely involved with dealing with primary sensory input.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior work.

claim: The 14A interneurons' NB is the persisting NB4-1 NB from the embryo.
source: More complex computations are likely carried out by the 14A interneurons. Their NB is the persisting NB4-1 NB from the embryo (Birkholz et al., 2015), and the homologous NB4-1 in grasshoppers produces the cluster of midline spiking interneurons (Shepherd and Laurent, 1992) that conveys information from the somatosensory map to the myotopic motor map (Burrows and Newland, 1993; Burrows, 1996).
evidence: This is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: The homologous NB4-1 in grasshoppers produces the cluster of midline spiking interneurons that conveys information from the somatosensory map to the myotopic motor map.
source: Their NB is the persisting NB4-1 NB from the embryo (Birkholz et al., 2015), and the homologous NB4-1 in grasshoppers produces the cluster of midline spiking interneurons (Shepherd and Laurent, 1992) that conveys information from the somatosensory map to the myotopic motor map (Burrows and Newland, 1993; Burrows, 1996).
evidence: This is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: The fly 14A neurons are anatomically similar to the grasshopper NB4-1 neurons and are expected to be involved in maintaining spatial information during the transformation from sensory to motor maps in the leg.
source: The neurons generated by NB 4-1 in flies are anatomically similar to the grasshopper neurons and we expect that the fly neurons are likewise involved in maintaining spatial information during the transformation from the sensory (Murphey et al., 1989) to motor maps (Brierley et al., 2012) in the leg.
evidence: This is an inference based on anatomical similarity and citations to published work.

claim: The tectulum neuropil is built from the dorsal-projecting lineages in the larva.
source: The tectulum neuropil is built from the dorsal-projecting lineages in the larva.
evidence: This is based on anatomical observations.

claim: As metamorphosis approaches, the segmental hemilineages begin to converge on the T2 region.
source: They arise as segmentally discrete units but as metamorphosis approaches the segmental hemilineages begin to converge on the T2 region.
evidence: This is based on developmental observations.

claim: Some hemilineages that project to the tectulum region appear relatively homogeneous (e.g., 6A and 6B), while others are more complex and contain obvious subclasses of interneurons (e.g., 12A and 8B).
source: For some of the dorsal-projecting hemilineages the members in the cluster appear relatively homogeneous (e.g., 6A and 6B), as seen for most of the leg hemilineages. In other instances, though, such as the 12A and 8B groups, the hemilineage cluster is more complex and contains obvious subclasses of interneurons.
evidence: This is based on anatomical observations.

claim: The more homogenous hemilineages are likely collections of parallel components providing parallel but overlapping channels in sensory to motor transformation circuits.
source: We speculate that the more homogenous hemilineages are collections of parallel components, which provide parallel but overlapping channels in the circuits that control sensory to motor transformations.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the anatomical observations.

claim: The more heterogeneous hemilineages likely have more diversified integrative functions.
source: The more heterogeneous hemilineages likely have more diversified integrative functions.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the anatomical observations.

claim: Many brain lineages in Drosophila contain a greater diversity of cell types than VNS hemilineages.
source: The recent characterization of lineages in the fly brain (Ito et al., 2013; Yu et al., 2013) shows many brain lineages that contain a greater diversity of cell types than we see for the VNS hemilineages.
evidence: This is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: Some brain lineages appear to be simple, rather homogeneous collections of neurons that represent parallel processing units.
source: Nevertheless, some of the brain lineages also appear to be simple, rather homogeneous collections of neurons and we would expect these to also represent parallel processing units.
evidence: This is an inference based on comparison with VNS hemilineages and brain lineage data.

claim: A projection neuron hemilineage from the lateral antennal lobe (lAL) NB contains five classes of projection neurons all involved in receiving primary sensory input and relaying it to higher centers.
source: This idea is supported by a projection neuron hemilineage from the lateral antennal lobe (lAL) NB. Overall, this hemilineage contains five classes of projection neurons but they are all involved in receiving primary sensory input (olfactory, gustatory, or primary antennal mechanosensory) and relaying it to higher centers within or around the mushroom bodies (Lin et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to published work.

claim: Most hemilineage lines had some degree of contamination with expression in neurons outside of the target hemilineage.
source: As summarized in Supplementary file 1, most of our lines had some degree of contamination with expression in neurons that were outside of our target hemilineage.
evidence: This is a statement about the experimental limitations of the study.

claim: Lines showing expression in sensory neurons (such as hemilineages 3A and 19B) were not used for behavioral studies.
source: We did not use lines that showed expression in sensory neurons (such as hemilineages 3A and 19B), or that had expression in other hemilineage clusters (e.g., the hemilineage 14A line).
evidence: This is a statement about experimental methodology.

claim: Decapitated flies showed a complex array of behaviors during the tests despite lacking their heads.
source: Despite lacking their heads, these flies showed a complex array of behaviors during the tests.
evidence: This is an observation from the behavioral experiments.

claim: Tonic responses were more common than sequential responses during TRPA1 activation.
source: Tonic responses were the more common and are defined as a persistent behavioral response that began at some point during the heat ramp and were then maintained for the remainder of the stimulus.
evidence: This is a summary of behavioral observations.

claim: Stimulation of 12A neurons caused decapitated flies to display an ordered sequence of behavioral responses that changed as temperature increased.
source: This was very evident for the stimulation of the 12A neurons that began with locomotion that was later joined by lateral wing waving and then finally by the onset of sustained wing buzzing.
evidence: This is a description of behavioral observations.

claim: The 9A and 5B clusters are GABA-immunopositive neurons.
source: We do not have detailed transmitter information for all of the hemilineage groups but we do know that the 9A and 5B clusters are GABA-immunopositive neurons (Harris, 2012).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior work.

claim: For hemilineages that evoked more complex behaviors, the response to stimulation was probabilistic rather than deterministic.
source: The hemilineages that evoked more complex behaviors typically showed a range of behaviors, although there was usually a dominant category of response that characterized that particular hemilineage group. Therefore, for these more complex behaviors, the response to hemilineage group stimulation was probabilistic rather than deterministic, in that the activity of these neurons enhanced the probability that a particular behavior would be performed.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from behavioral observations.

claim: Larval Drosophila behavioral responses to TRPA1 activation of different sparse sets of central neurons tended to be probabilistic.
source: A similar phenomenon was seen in the behavioral responses of larval Drosophila to TRPA1 activation of different sparse sets of central neurons (Vogelstein et al., 2014). The larval behavioral responses also tended to be probabilistic in that a given set of neurons enhanced the probability of a behavioral response but their activity did not invariably lead to this response.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to published work.

claim: Hemilineage groups that evoke changes in leg posture have their arbors concentrated in the leg neuropils.
source: Not surprisingly, the hemilineage groups that evoke changes in leg posture have their arbors concentrated in the leg neuropils.
evidence: This is a correlation between anatomical and behavioral data shown in Figure 9.

claim: Hemilineages that evoke coordinated or uncoordinated leg movements have a strong leg neuropil component but their arbors also project into the medial neuropil and into the tectulum neuropil.
source: Hemilineages that evoke coordinated or uncoordinated leg movements similarly have a strong leg neuropil component but their arbors also project into the medial neuropil and into the tectulum neuropil.
evidence: This is a correlation between anatomical and behavioral data shown in Figure 9.

claim: Strong projections into the tectulum neuropil were evident for all hemilineages that evoked wing movements of either low or high frequency.
source: Strong projections into the tectulum neuropil were also evident for all of the hemilineages that evoked wing movements of either low or high frequency.
evidence: This is a correlation between anatomical and behavioral data shown in Figure 9.

claim: Two of the three hemilineages that evoked frequent takeoff had a strong projection into the T2 leg neuropil in addition to their extensive arbor in the tectulum.
source: Two of the three hemilineages that evoked frequent takeoff had a strong projection into the T2 leg neuropil (the site of the jump motoneurons) in addition to their extensive arbor in the tectulum.
evidence: This is a correlation between anatomical and behavioral data shown in Figure 9.

claim: The third takeoff lineage, lineage 11A/B, lacked a T2 arbor but had substantial projections into the T1 and T3 leg neuropils.
source: Curiously, the third takeoff lineage, lineage 11A/B, lacked a T2 arbor but had substantial projections into the T1 and T3 leg neuropils.
evidence: This is an anatomical observation shown in Figure 9.

claim: The leg neuropils deal with leg function while the tectulum neuropil is involved with wing-related behavior such as singing or flight.
source: Overall the anatomy of the hemilineages conformed to the generally held idea that the leg neuropils deal with leg function while the tectulum neuropil is involved with wing-related behavior such as singing or flight.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from correlating anatomical and behavioral data with established knowledge.

claim: The tectulum and dorsomedial neuropil may be generally involved in complex, coordinated behavior in the thorax.
source: In addition, though, the tectulum and dorsomedial neuropil may be generally involved in complex, coordinated behavior in the thorax.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from anatomical and behavioral observations.

claim: Hemilineages such as 1A and 10B that evoke walking behavior but little wing movement have arbor extension into the dorsomedial neuropil and tectulum.
source: Hemilineages, such as 1A and 10B, that evoke walking behavior but little in the way of wing movement nevertheless have arbor extension into the dorsomedial neuropil and tectulum, suggesting that these regions may be generally involved in the coordination of complex thoracic behavior regardless of whether it involves legs or wings.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from anatomical and behavioral observations.

claim: Hemilineages appear to have a modular function with cells in a given group being associated with particular behavioral responses.
source: Overall the hemilineages appear to have a modular function with cells in a given group being associated with particular behavioral responses.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental observations.

claim: In grasshoppers, computational circuits are built from clusters of distinct types of interneurons, at least some of which arise in the same lineage.
source: This notion is consistent with physiological data such as that from grasshoppers in which computational circuits are built from clusters of distinct types of interneurons (Burrows, 1996), at least some types of which have been shown to arise in the same lineage (Shepherd and Laurent, 1992).
evidence: This is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: In the vertebrate spinal cord, different cell types arise from defined sets of precursors and play specific roles in defined circuit motifs.
source: A similar strategy is seen in the vertebrate spinal cord in which different cell types arise from defined sets of precursors and the neurons from those cell types play specific roles in defined circuit motifs (Grillner and Jessell, 2009).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to published work.

claim: The vPR6 neurons are required for song production in the male.
source: A second caution comes from our demonstration that the vPR6 neurons, which are required for song production in the male (von Philipsborn et al., 2011), are part of hemilineage 12A cluster (Figure 7).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to published work and data shown in Figure 7.

claim: The segmental CNS of insects provides an unparalleled system to study the evolution and diversification of the nervous system.
source: The segmental CNS of insects provides an unparalleled system in which to study the evolution and diversification of the nervous system.
evidence: This is a general statement about the advantages of the insect system.

claim: The stereotyped array of segmental NBs in insects has undergone little change through the course of insect evolution.
source: The advantage of the insect system lies in a stereotyped array of segmental NBs that has undergone little change through the course of insect evolution.
evidence: This is based on established knowledge about insect evolution.

claim: Homologous stem cells can be identified in insects as diverse as silverfish, grasshoppers and Drosophila based on position, molecular markers and early progeny.
source: Based on position, molecular markers and the types of early progeny that they produce, the homologous stem cells can be identified in insects as diverse as silverfish, grasshoppers and Drosophila (Thomas et al., 1984; Truman and Ball, 1998).
evidence: This is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: The early neuronal progeny of NBs are highly conserved across insects.
source: Not only have the NBs been highly conserved, but their early neuronal progeny are also highly conserved as first elegantly shown by Thomas et al. (1984).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to published work.

claim: The early-born 'primary' neurons have identities determined by birth-order as encoded in a transcription factor progression within the cycling NB.
source: These early-born cells are the 'primary' neurons and their identities are determined by birth-order as encoded in a transcription factor progression within the cycling NB (Isshiki et al., 2001).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to published work.

claim: Many early-born cells serve a pioneer function, explaining the stereotyped pattern of tracts and commissures seen in the ventral neuropil throughout insects.
source: Many of these early-born cells serve a pioneer function, which explains the stereotyped pattern of tracts and commissures seen in the ventral neuropil throughout the insects (Thomas et al., 1984).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to published work.

claim: Later-born 'secondary' neurons are born after the NB starts to express grainyhead and include late-born embryonic neurons and all postembryonic neurons.
source: The later-born 'secondary' neurons are born after the NB starts to express grainyhead (Almeida and Bray, 2005) and include late-born embryonic neurons as well as all of the neurons that are born during postembryonic life (see Zhou et al., 2009; for a discussion of primary vs secondary neurons).
evidence: This is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: In grasshoppers, the medial lineage A hemilineage cells are GABAergic, engrailed-positive local interneurons and the B hemilineage cells are engrailed-negative projection cells.
source: Conservation in class character in widely different groups is well illustrated by the medial lineage. In grasshoppers the A hemilineage cells are GABAergic, engrailed-positive local interneurons and the B hemilineage cells are engrailed-negative, projection cells (Jia and Siegler, 2002), and the same is true in Drosophila (JW Truman, unpublished).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to published work and unpublished observations.

claim: In Drosophila, the medial lineage A hemilineage cells are GABAergic, engrailed-positive local interneurons and the B hemilineage cells are engrailed-negative projection cells.
source: Conservation in class character in widely different groups is well illustrated by the medial lineage. In grasshoppers the A hemilineage cells are GABAergic, engrailed-positive local interneurons and the B hemilineage cells are engrailed-negative, projection cells (Jia and Siegler, 2002), and the same is true in Drosophila (JW Truman, unpublished).
evidence: This is based on unpublished observations.

claim: A comparative analysis of GABA-immunoreactive neurons in the VNS of diverse insects supports the contention that the properties of neurons in homologous hemilineages are highly conserved across much of the insects.
source: Similarly, a comparative analysis of the clusters of GABA-immunoreactive neurons in the VNS of diverse insects (Witten and Truman, 1998) supports the contention that the properties of neurons in homologous hemilineages are highly conserved across much of the insects.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to published work.

claim: It is unlikely that one could homologize individual neurons within a particular class across insects.
source: Although one can homologize cell classes of secondary neurons across most of the insects, we think that it is unlikely that one could homologize individual neurons within a particular class.
evidence: This is a speculative statement based on the authors' interpretation.

claim: In grasshoppers, ventral interneurons that run in the transverse tract receive input from wing afferents.
source: In grasshoppers ventral interneurons that run in the transverse tract receive input from wing afferents (Watson and Burrows, 1983) while in flies the 2A interneurons are the main neurons of the transverse tract and they can drive flight behavior.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to published work.

claim: In flies, the 2A interneurons are the main neurons of the transverse tract and they can drive flight behavior.
source: In grasshoppers ventral interneurons that run in the transverse tract receive input from wing afferents (Watson and Burrows, 1983) while in flies the 2A interneurons are the main neurons of the transverse tract and they can drive flight behavior.
evidence: This is based on anatomical and behavioral observations from this study.

claim: In grasshoppers, NB4-1 and NB3-1 make the medial and anteromedial spiking interneurons, respectively, of the leg circuit.
source: For the leg hemilineages, NB4-1 and NB3-1 in grasshopper make the medial and anteromedial spiking interneurons, respectively, of the leg circuit (Burrows, 1996), while in flies the homologous NBs (Truman et al., 2004) generate the 14A and 4B interneurons which are similar appearing local interneurons in the leg neuropil.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to published work.

claim: In flies, the homologous NBs to grasshopper NB4-1 and NB3-1 generate the 14A and 4B interneurons which are similar appearing local interneurons in the leg neuropil.
source: For the leg hemilineages, NB4-1 and NB3-1 in grasshopper make the medial and anteromedial spiking interneurons, respectively, of the leg circuit (Burrows, 1996), while in flies the homologous NBs (Truman et al., 2004) generate the 14A and 4B interneurons which are similar appearing local interneurons in the leg neuropil.
evidence: This is based on anatomical observations and a citation to prior work.

claim: The functional roles of most or all of the hemilineages are expected to be highly conserved through much of insect evolution.
source: We expect that the functional roles of most of all of the hemilineages to be highly conserved through much of insect evolution.
evidence: This is a speculative statement based on the authors' interpretation of the data.

claim: For simpler hemilineages with parallel units, addition or reduction in neuron numbers could enhance or reduce functionality by altering spatial or temporal resolution.
source: For the simpler hemilineages that contain units that work in parallel, addition or reductions in the number of neurons could enhance or reduce functionality by altering the spatial or temporal resolution of their level of the computational network.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about evolutionary mechanisms.

claim: An increase in numbers of an interneuron type could provide finer control over the speed of locomotion, as seen for swimming speed control in larval zebrafish.
source: Another benefit of an increase in numbers of an interneuron type could be to provide a finer control over the speed of locomotion , as seen for the control of swimming speed in larval zebrafish (McLean et al., 2008) in which the increase in speed involves the recruitment of new interneurons and the repression of interneurons active at the slower speed.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to published work.

claim: For higher level, more complex hemilineages, changes in neuronal properties/connectivity rather than numbers might be more important for generating behavioral changes.
source: For higher level, more complex hemilineages, changes in neuronal properties/connectivity rather than numbers might be more important for generating behavioral changes.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about evolutionary mechanisms.

claim: The flight system of Drosophila, with its mesothoracic wings and metathoracic halteres, is a highly derived system compared with more basal insect groups.
source: It is important to remember, though, that the flight system of Drosophila, with its mesothoracic wings and metathoracic halteres, is a highly derived system compared with more basal insect groups.
evidence: This is based on established knowledge about insect evolution.

claim: About a third of the thoracic hemilineages die in the fly, leaving few if any members.
source: Also, in the fly about a third of the thoracic hemilineages die leaving few if any members (Truman et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to published work.

claim: Some cell types that may have been important in the ancestral nervous system have been lost with the evolution of Drosophila's derived pattern of flight.
source: Consequently, some cell types that may have been important in the ancestral nervous system have been lost with the evolution of Drosophila's derived pattern of flight.
evidence: This is an inference based on evolutionary considerations.

claim: The analysis includes only the postembryonic secondary neurons, lacking access to the embryonic-born neurons.
source: The other important caveat is that our analysis includes only the postembryonic secondary neurons, and so we are lacking access to the embryonic-born neurons, a small but extremely important component of the adult CNS.
evidence: This is a statement about the limitations of the study.

claim: A thoracic unit of the fly thoracic nervous system has about 2500 pairs of neurons, most of which can be assigned to 33 hemilineage units.
source: However, a thoracic unit of the fly thoracic nervous system has about 2500 pairs of neurons, most of which can be assigned to 33 hemilineage units.
evidence: This is a quantitative statement about the thoracic nervous system.

claim: Hemilineage 1A neurons are projection neurons that travel through the vA commissure and form one of the most ventral tracts in the VNS.
source: The adult 1A interneurons, by contrast, are projection neurons that travel through the vA commissure and form one of the most ventral tracts in the VNS (Figure 4A,B).
evidence: This is supported by anatomical data shown in Figure 4.

claim: After crossing the midline, the 1A bundle makes a distinctive posterior 'hook' and then bifurcates into dorsal and ventrolateral projections.
source: After crossing the midline, the 1A bundle makes a distinctive posterior 'hook' (Figure 4A) and then bifurcates into dorsal and ventrolateral projections (Figure 4B, Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by anatomical data shown in Figure 4.

claim: nSynaptotagmin::GFP localizes primarily in the ventral arbors of 1A neurons in the intermediate layers of the leg neuropil, showing the primary output regions of these cells.
source: A synaptotagmin::GFP fusion protein (nSyt::GFP) (Zhang et al., 2002; Pfeiffer et al., 2010; Seelig and Jayaraman, 2013) localizes primarily in the ventral arbors (Figure 4C) in the intermediate layers of the leg neuropil, showing the primary output regions of these cells.
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 4C and citations to published methods.

claim: Activation of 1A interneurons via TRPA1 evoked forward locomotion in decapitated flies.
source: Activation of 1A interneurons via TRPA1 evoked forward locomotion.
evidence: This is a behavioral observation from the experiments.

claim: During 1A activation, leg movements were erratic and not organized in the tripod gait typical of walking in intact flies, but there was clear intersegmental coordination of the limbs.
source: During locomotion the leg movements were erratic and not organized in the tripod gait typical of walking in intact flies (Strauss and Heisenberg, 1990), but there was clear intersegmental coordination of the limbs.
evidence: This is a behavioral observation with a citation to published work on normal walking.

claim: The 2A interneurons extend broadly within the ipsilateral part of the tectulum.
source: This anatomy is conserved in the adult, with the 2A interneurons extending broadly within the ipsilateral part of the tectulum (Figure 4G–I).
evidence: This is supported by anatomical data shown in Figure 4.

claim: Activation of the 2A interneurons drove high frequency wing movements in 54% of decapitated flies (n = 25).
source: Activation of the 2A interneurons drove high frequency wing movements (54%, n = 25).
evidence: This is a quantitative behavioral observation.

claim: During 2A activation, decapitated flies typically stood in place but abruptly initiated high frequency flapping with wings extended laterally in the flight position as temperature increased.
source: The decapitated flies typically stood in place but as the temperature increased, they abruptly initiated high frequency flapping with the wings extended laterally in the flight position (Figure 4J; Video 3).
evidence: This is a behavioral observation supported by Figure 4J and Video 3.

claim: In the adult, the cell bodies of hemilineage 3A remain ventral, just posterior to the leg nerve insertion and their arbors extend through intermediate levels of the leg neuropil.
source: In the adult, the cell bodies of hemilineage 3A remain ventral, just posterior to the leg nerve insertion and their arbors extend through intermediate levels of the leg neuropil (Figure 4K,L).
evidence: This is supported by anatomical data shown in Figure 4.

claim: The cluster of 3B interneurons is severely reduced or absent in T3.
source: The cluster of 3B interneurons is severely reduced or absent in T3.
evidence: This is an anatomical observation.

claim: In T1 and T2, the arbors of 3B cells converge in the tectulum to form a complex arbor in the very dorsal layer of this neuropil.
source: In T1 and T2 the arbors of the cells converge in the tectulum to form a complex arbor (Figure 4M,N) in the very dorsal layer of this neuropil.
evidence: This is supported by anatomical data shown in Figure 4.

claim: Activation of 3B interneurons caused decapitated flies to show subtle repositioning of legs, repetitive poorly coordinated leg movements, occasional grooming bouts, and occasional wing flicking and scissoring movements but not high frequency wing buzzing.
source: As the temperature ramped up, the decapitated flies showed a subtle repositioning of the legs, with some repetitive, poorly coordinated leg movements and occasional grooming bouts. They also performed occasional wing flicking and wing scissoring movements but did not show high frequency wing buzzing.
evidence: This is a behavioral observation from the experiments.

claim: In the adult, the 5B cell bodies are pulled towards the midline and their bundled axons cross the midline in the iP commissure, forming a major ipsilateral arbor just prior to crossing.
source: In the adult, the cell bodies are pulled towards the midline. Their bundled axons cross the midline in the iP commissure, and form a major ipsilateral arbor just prior to crossing (Figure 4P,Q).
evidence: This is supported by anatomical data shown in Figure 4.

claim: When 5B interneurons were activated, decapitated flies showed a progressive repositioning of their limbs so that they were closer to the ground by the end of the thermal ramp.
source: When the 5B interneurons were activated, the decapitated flies showed a progressive repositioning of their limbs so that they are closer to the ground by the end of the thermal ramp (Figure 4R, Video 5).
evidence: This is a behavioral observation supported by Figure 4R and Video 5.

claim: Tethered intact flies gripping a Styrofoam ball responded to 5B activation by lowering their body position, drawing the ball closer to them.
source: Tethered intact flies that were gripping a Styrofoam ball responded to the temperature ramp by lowering their body position, thereby drawing the ball closer to them (Figure 4S).
evidence: This is a behavioral observation supported by Figure 4S.

claim: Hemilineage 6A clusters are found in neuromeres S3 through A1 and form one of the dorsalmost arbors of the tectulum.
source: Hemilineage 6A clusters are found in neuromeres S3 through A1 (Figure 5A) and form one of the dorsalmost arbors of the tectulum.
evidence: This is supported by anatomical data shown in Figure 5.

claim: The 6A clusters show an ipsilateral arbor largely confined to the segment of origin and a distal, contralateral arbor that converges from S3 through A1 into the T2 region of the tectulum.
source: The 6A clusters show an ipsilateral arbor that is largely confined to the segment of origin and a distal, contralateral arbor that converges from S3 through A1 into the T2 region of the tectulum (Figure 5A,B).
evidence: This is supported by anatomical data shown in Figure 5.

claim: nSyt::GFP localizes to the lateral portions of the contralateral arbor of 6A neurons.
source: nSyt::GFP localizes to the lateral portions of the contralateral arbor (Figure 5C).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 5C.

claim: The neurons of 6B cluster are found in T1 to T3 but typically are missing from segment A1.
source: The neurons of 6B cluster are found in T1 to T3 but typically are missing from segment A1.
evidence: This is an anatomical observation.

claim: The 6B bundle crosses in the iP commissure without an ipsilateral arbor and then branches profusely in the tectulum neuropil and the dorsal-most region of the leg neuropils.
source: The 6B bundle crosses in the iP commissure without an ipsilateral arbor and then branches profusely in the tectulum neuropil and the dorsal-most region of the leg neuropils (Figure 5E,F).
evidence: This is supported by anatomical data shown in Figure 5.

claim: Activation of 6A interneurons started with poorly coordinated leg movements that often pitched the fly forward onto its anterior thorax, followed by very erratic movements.
source: Activation of the 6A interneurons via the heat ramp started with poorly coordinated movements of the legs that often pitched the fly forward onto its anterior thorax (Figure 6D, Video 6). The movements were not organized into any particular direction and became very erratic towards the end (Figure 6D, 30-31s).
evidence: This is a behavioral observation supported by Figure 6D and Video 6.

claim: Activation of 6B interneurons in decapitated flies elicited a mixture of leg-related movements, with some showing curving forward movement while others pivoted in place.
source: Activation of the 6B interneurons in the decapitated flies elicited a mixture of leg-related movements (Figure 5G; Video 7). Some showed a curving, forward movement while others pivoted in place.
evidence: This is a behavioral observation supported by Figure 5G and Video 7.

claim: The 7B neurite projects dorsally, forming a bushy ipsilateral arbor in the tectulum, then crosses the midline to form an ascending tract that extends through the neck connective.
source: The neurite projects dorsally, forming a bushy ipsilateral (proximal) arbor in the tectulum, then crosses the midline to form an ascending tract that extends through the neck connective (Figure 5H).
evidence: This is supported by anatomical data shown in Figure 5.

claim: The arbor of 7B neurons in the T2 hemineuromere includes prominent projections into the dorsolateral region of the T2 leg neuropil.
source: The arbor in the T2 hemineuromere includes prominent projections into the dorsolateral region of the T2 leg neuropil (Figure 5I).
evidence: This is supported by anatomical data shown in Figure 5.

claim: Gradual activation of 7B interneurons by the heat ramp resulted in little walking behavior, with decapitated flies continuing spontaneous grooming with occasional wing flicking until they abruptly launched into the air.
source: The gradual activation of the 7B interneurons by the heat ramp resulted in little walking behavior. The decapitated flies continued spontaneous grooming with occasional wing flicking behavior until they abruptly launch themselves into the air (Video 8).
evidence: This is a behavioral observation supported by Video 8.

claim: High speed video analysis shows that 7B activation behavior corresponds to the normal takeoff sequence: wings raised, mesothoracic legs extend in a jump, wings depress and fly begins to flap.
source: High speed video analysis (Figure 5J, Video 9) shows that their behavior corresponds to the normal takeoff sequence described by Card and Dickinson (2008): first the wings are raised, the mesothoracic legs then extend in a jump, and finally the wings depress and the fly begins to flap.
evidence: This is supported by high-speed video data shown in Figure 5J and Video 9, with a citation to published work on normal takeoff.

claim: In the adult, the 8A somata are found in approximately the same location as in the larva; their bundled neurites make a pronounced lateral bend after entering the neuropil and form prominent arbors that ramify through the lateral portion of the ipsilateral leg neuropil.
source: In the adult, the 8A somata are found in approximately the same location; their bundled neurites make a pronounced lateral bend after they enter the neuropil and form prominent arbors that ramify through the lateral portion of the ipsilateral leg neuropil (Figure 5K,L).
evidence: This is supported by anatomical data shown in Figure 5.

claim: The 8B cluster in the adult contains multi-part, midline-crossing, intersegmental arbors.
source: The 8B cluster in the adult contains multi-part, midline-crossing, intersegmental arbors (Figure 5N).
evidence: This is supported by anatomical data shown in Figure 5.

claim: A prominent component of the T3 lineage 8B are the contralateral haltere interneurons (cHINs) with their distinctive 'bowtie' arbor.
source: A prominent component of the T3 lineage are the contralateral haltere interneurons (cHINs; Strausfeld and Seyan, 1985), with their distinctive 'bowtie' arbor (Figure 5N,O).
evidence: This is supported by anatomical data shown in Figure 5 and a citation to published work.

claim: The cHINs receive sensory inputs from the haltere nerve on their lower, intrasegmental ipsilateral arbor, and then make an ascending contralateral projection.
source: These neurons receive sensory inputs from the haltere nerve, on their lower, intrasegmental ipsilateral arbor, and then make an ascending contralateral projection.
evidence: This is based on anatomical observations.

claim: Activation of 8A interneurons had minimal effects on the behavior of decapitated flies, with little effect on spontaneous behavior and no walking or wing movements.
source: Activation of the 8A interneurons using line R69H11-GAL4 had minimal effects on the behavior of the decapitated flies (Figure 5M, Video 10). As the temperature ramped up, we saw little effect on spontaneous behavior. The flies continued to show bouts of grooming; they also showed fidgety repositioning of their legs, but no walking or wing movements.
evidence: This is a behavioral observation supported by Figure 5M and Video 10.

claim: In the adult, 9A somata are found in the middle third of the VNS and are local leg interneurons that arborize in the ventral leg neuropil.
source: In the adult, the 9A somata are found in the middle third of the VNS. They are local leg interneurons that arborize in the ventral leg neuropil (Figure 5P,Q), as described in Brown and Truman (2009).
evidence: This is supported by anatomical data shown in Figure 5 and a citation to published work.

claim: The 9A neurons overlap with afferents from leg chordotonal organs.
source: These neurons overlap with afferents from leg chordotonal organs (Harris, 2012).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior work.

claim: Activation of 9A interneurons resulted in a subtle change in posture in decapitated flies as their legs became gradually more splayed out during the heat ramp.
source: Activation of the 9A interneurons resulted in a subtle change in posture in the decapitated flies as their legs became gradually more splayed out during the course of the heat ramp (Figure 5R, Video 11).
evidence: This is a behavioral observation supported by Figure 5R and Video 11.

claim: The hemilineage 10B cell bodies remain anteromedial in the adult, and their primary neurites cross the midline in an iA bundle and form a finger-like ventral arbor and an intersegmental dorsal arbor.
source: The hemilineage 10B cell bodies remain anteromedial in the adult. Their primary neurites cross the midline in an iA bundle and form a finger-like ventral arbor, which starts medial and projects ventrally almost to the leg nerve insertion, and an intersegmental dorsal arbor running just lateral to the midline (Figure 6B).
evidence: This is supported by anatomical data shown in Figure 6.

claim: The behavioral responses of decapitated flies to activation of 10B interneurons were dominated by leg movements that were somewhat erratic, often causing pivoting movements, and when there was net movement, it was usually backwards.
source: The behavioral responses of decapitated flies to the activation of the 10B interneurons were dominated by leg movements (Figure 6C; Video 12). These movements were somewhat erratic, often causing the flies to make pivoting movements around a leg. When there was net movement, it was usually backwards.
evidence: This is a behavioral observation supported by Figure 6C and Video 12.

claim: Lineage 11A is found in T1 and T2, whereas lineage 11B is found only in T2.
source: Lineage 11A is found in T1 and T2, whereas lineage 11B is found only in T2.
evidence: This is an anatomical observation.

claim: In the adult, the lineage 11 cell bodies are in the dorsoposterior margin of T1 and T2, and the neurons show a complex projection that is predominantly in T2 and largely confined to the tectulum neuropil.
source: In the adult, the lineage 11 cell bodies are in the dorsoposterior margin of T1 and T2. The lineage 11 neurons show a complex projection that is predominantly in T2 and largely confined to the tectulum neuropil (Figure 6D,E).
evidence: This is supported by anatomical data shown in Figure 6.

claim: Similar to 7B interneurons, activation of lineage 11 interneurons evoked takeoff behavior.
source: Similar to the 7B interneurons, the activation of the lineage 11 interneurons using R26B05-GAL4 evoked takeoff behavior.
evidence: This is a behavioral observation.

claim: High-speed video analysis showed that the behavioral sequencing of lineage 11 activation differed from normal takeoff in that decapitated flies commenced wing flapping prior to the jump.
source: High-speed video analysis showed that the behavioral sequencing differed from normal takeoff in that the decapitated flies commenced wing flapping prior to the jump (Figure 6F, Video 13).
evidence: This is supported by high-speed video data shown in Figure 6F and Video 13.

claim: Using tsh-GAL80 to suppress thoracic expression while leaving expression in descending interneurons showed a severe reduction in takeoffs (9% vs 100%), indicating that thoracic lineage 11 neurons drive the takeoff behavior.
source: Consequently, we used teashirt-GAL80 (tsh-GAL80; Clyne and Miesenböck, 2008) to suppress thoracic expression, but leaving expression in the descending interneurons (Figure 6—figure supplement 1B). These decapitated flies showed a severe reduction in the number of takeoffs when subjected to the heat ramp (9% of tsh-GAL80 flies [N = 22] vs 100% [N = 13] for R26B05-GAL4 flies lacking the tsh-GAL80).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1 and a citation to the tsh-GAL80 method.

claim: Hemilineage 12A arborizes throughout the dorsal tectulum neuropil, with arbors from T1 and T2 clusters converging on T2 and extensively overlapping.
source: Hemilineage 12A arborizes throughout the dorsal tectulum neuropil. The arbors from the T1 and T2 clusters converge on T2 and extensively overlap (Figure 6G,H).
evidence: This is supported by anatomical data shown in Figure 6.

claim: nSyT::GFP localizes to the medial portions of the dorsal arbors of 12A neurons, plus a small region in the lateral part of the lower arbors.
source: nSyT::GFP localizes to the medial portions of the dorsal arbors, plus a small region in the lateral part of the lower arbors (Figure 6I).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 6I.

claim: The mature 12B neurons have no ipsilateral arbor and cross the midline in the pI commissure to arborize in the medial region of the contralateral leg neuropil.
source: The mature 12B neurons have no ipsilateral arbor and cross the midline in the pI commissure to arborize in the medial region of the contralateral leg neuropil (Figure 6K,L).
evidence: This is supported by anatomical data shown in Figure 6.

claim: Activation of 12A interneurons produced a sequence of behaviors as temperature ramped up: walking, then wing flicking and lateral extension/vibration of a single wing, eventually extreme frequency wing vibrations usually not in flight position.
source: Activation of the 12A interneurons produced a sequence of behaviors as the temperature ramped up (Figure 6J; Video 14). The decapitated flies started with walking behavior that was later joined by wing flicking and by the lateral extension and vibration of a single wing (Figure 6J, 30°C), resembling the courtship singing of the male. Eventually the frequency of wing vibrations became extreme but the wings were usually not extended in the flight position; often one vibrating wing was partially or fully extended to the side while the other was vibrating while over the back (Figure 6J, 35°C).
evidence: This is a behavioral observation supported by Figure 6J and Video 14.

claim: Activation of 12B interneurons had little effect on some decapitated flies but evoked a tonic postural change in others, with T2 and T3 legs undergoing extreme extension and freezing in this position.
source: In contrast to the 12A cells, the activation of the 12B interneurons had little effect on some decapitated flies but evoked a tonic postural change in others. The T2 and T3 legs underwent an extreme extension and the legs froze in this position (Figure 6M,N, Video 15).
evidence: This is a behavioral observation supported by Figure 6M,N and Video 15.

claim: In the adult, the 13A neurons insert into the neuropil near the entry of the leg nerve and their arbors extend along the edges of the leg neuropil and ramify through its ventral half.
source: In the adult, the 13A neurons insert into the neuropil near the entry of the leg nerve. Their arbors extend along the edges of the leg neuropil and ramify through its ventral half (Figure 6O,P).
evidence: This is supported by anatomical data shown in Figure 6.

claim: The cell bodies of 13B cluster are pulled medially during metamorphosis and sometimes are pulled across the midline.
source: The cell bodies of 13B cluster are pulled medially during metamorphosis and sometimes are pulled across the midline (Figure 6Q).
evidence: This is supported by anatomical data shown in Figure 6.

claim: The 13B neurons' axons cross the midline in the vA commissure and constitute the ventral-most bundle, branching extensively through the ventral region of the leg neuropil.
source: Their axons cross the midline in the vA commissure and constitute the ventral-most bundle (Figure 6R). The 13B neurons branch extensively through the ventral region of the leg neuropil.
evidence: This is supported by anatomical data shown in Figure 6.

claim: Activation of 13B cells in decapitated flies evoked a tonic postural change, with flies progressively extending their legs more to the side so that by the end of the heat ramp they were often resting on their coxae with tarsi elevated into the air.
source: Activation of the 13B cells in decapitated flies evoked a tonic postural change. As the temperature increased they extended their legs progressively more to the side so that by the end of the heat ramp they were often resting on their coxae, with their tarsi elevated into the air (Figure 6S,T; Video 16).
evidence: This is a behavioral observation supported by Figure 6S,T and Video 16.

claim: In lineage 14, most of the 14B neurons die, so the cluster is comprised almost exclusively of hemilineage 14A neurons.
source: In lineage 14, most of the 14B neurons die, so the cluster is comprised almost exclusively of hemilineage 14A neurons (Truman et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to published work.

claim: During metamorphosis, the cell clusters of 14A neurons are pulled to the anterior midline, and their axons form an extreme ventral bundle just dorsal and anterior to the 13B neurons.
source: During metamorphosis the cell clusters of the 14A neurons are pulled to the anterior midline. Their axons form an extreme ventral bundle that is just dorsal and anterior to the 13B neurons.
evidence: This is an anatomical observation.

claim: The 14A neurons have no ipsilateral arbor and arborize throughout the ventral half of the leg neuropil and also laterally in the region where the motoneurons arborize.
source: The 14A neurons have no ipsilateral arbor and arborize throughout the ventral half of the leg neuropil and also laterally in the region where the motoneurons arborize (Figure 6U,V).
evidence: This is supported by anatomical data shown in Figure 6.

claim: Hemilineage 15B is one of the two major lineages that make leg motoneurons.
source: This is one of the two major lineages that make leg motoneurons (Figure 7A,B).
evidence: This is supported by anatomical data shown in Figure 7.

claim: The adult composition of hemilineage 15B has been extensively characterized, and they primarily supply muscles of the distal leg segments.
source: The adult composition of this lineage has been extensively characterized (Baek and Mann, 2009; Brierley et al., 2012) and they primarily supply muscles of the distal leg segments.
evidence: This is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: Hemilineage 18B is missing from T1 and only the 18B hemilineage persists in T2 and T3.
source: Lineage 18 is missing from T1 and only the 18B hemilineage persists in T2 and T3 (Truman et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to published work.

claim: The adult 18B projection pattern is complex, with cells projecting through much of the tectulum neuropil.
source: The adult projection pattern is complex as the cells project through much of the tectulum neuropil (Figure 7C,D).
evidence: This is supported by anatomical data shown in Figure 7.

claim: The T2 neurons of 18B show a concentration of arbor in the dorsal-most regions of the tectulum and also project a ventral arbor into the dorsolateral regions of the leg neuropils, a region occupied by the dendrites of the leg motoneurons.
source: The T2 neurons show a concentration of arbor in the dorsal-most regions of the tectulum and also project a ventral arbor into the dorsolateral regions of the leg neuropils, a region occupied by the dendrites of the leg motoneurons.
evidence: This is an anatomical observation.

claim: In response to activation of 18B neurons by the heat ramp, decapitated flies typically initiated walking sometimes accompanied by jerky wing movements, followed by a jump and transition to flapping, but not consistently in that order.
source: In response to the activation of the 18B neurons by the heat ramp, the decapitated flies typically initiated walking and that was sometimes accompanied by jerky wing movements with the wings remaining partially folded. After a latent period (varying from milliseconds to seconds), the fly would jump and the wing movements would transition into flapping, but not consistently in that order (Figure 7E; Video 17).
evidence: This is a behavioral observation supported by Figure 7E and Video 17.

claim: The adult 19A neurons project into the ipsilateral leg neuropil, forming a major projection extending through lateral and ventral leg neuropil and a medial projection that extends to the midline.
source: The 19A neurons project into the ipsilateral leg neuropil, where they form a major projection extending through lateral and ventral leg neuropil and a medial projection that extends to the midline.
evidence: This is an anatomical observation.

claim: The medial projections of 19A neurons in T1 and T2 converge on the midline in T2.
source: The medial projections in T1 and T2 converge on the midline in T2 (Figure 7F,G).
evidence: This is supported by anatomical data shown in Figure 7.

claim: nSyt::GFP localizes to the most medial (distal) part of the medial projection of 19A neurons.
source: nSyt::GFP localizes to the most medial (distal) part of the medial projection (Figure 7H).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 7H.

claim: The hemilineage 19B cluster in T1 is greatly reduced in the larva, and after metamorphosis the 19B cluster in T3 is also very small, presumably through cell death during metamorphosis.
source: The hemilineage 19B cluster in T1 is greatly reduced in the larva, and after metamorphosis the 19B cluster in T3 is also very small, presumably through cell death during metamorphosis.
evidence: This is an anatomical observation with a speculative explanation.

claim: The adult T2 neurons of 19B make a robust projection across the iP commissure and arborize dorsally in the tectulum neuropil, with both medial and lateral arbors that project anteriorly.
source: The adult T2 neurons make a robust projection across the iP commissure and arborize dorsally in the tectulum neuropil. The 19B neurons have both medial and lateral arbors that project anteriorly (Figure 7J,K; Figure 7—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by anatomical data shown in Figure 7.

claim: During activation of 19A interneurons, decapitated flies stayed in place and showed no movements of their T1 or T3 legs, but their T2 legs showed incessant waving movements that continued for the duration of thermal activation.
source: During activation of the 19A interneurons the decapitated flies stayed in place and showed no movements of their T1 or T3 legs, but their T2 legs show incessant waving movements that continue for the duration of the thermal activation (Figure 7I; Video 18).
evidence: This is a behavioral observation supported by Figure 7I and Video 18.

claim: In the larva, 20A and 22A are adjoining lineages in the posterior half of the neuromere, and their first few B progeny become motoneurons but the remainder die.
source: In the larva, 20A and 22A are adjoining lineages in the posterior half of the neuromere. Their first few B progeny become motoneurons but the remainder die (Truman et al. 2010).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to published work.

claim: The A progeny of both 20A and 22A NBs send very short projections to the ventral leg neuropil, and it is difficult to tell them apart.
source: The A progeny of both NBs send very short projections to the ventral leg neuropil, and it is difficult to tell them apart.
evidence: This is an anatomical observation.

claim: The cell body clusters for 20A/22A are found at the posteriolateral border of each thoracic segment and project anteriorly into the mid region of the leg neuropil, making a robust lateral branch and a thinner medial branch that extends into dorsal leg neuropil.
source: The cell body clusters for 20A/22A are found at the posteriolateral border of each thoracic segment (Figure 7L). The clusters project anteriorly into the mid region of the leg neuropil and then make a robust lateral branch and a thinner medial branch that extends into dorsal leg neuropil (Figure 7M).
evidence: This is supported by anatomical data shown in Figure 7.

claim: Activation of 20A/22A interneurons evoked a simple change in posture in decapitated flies, with flies extending their legs until they assumed a splayed out posture as temperature increased.
source: Activation of the 20A/22A interneurons evoked a simple change in posture in the decapitated flies. As the temperature increased, the flies extended their legs until they had assumed a splayed out posture (Figure 7N; Video 19).
evidence: This is a behavioral observation supported by Figure 7N and Video 19.

claim: In the adult, the cell body cluster of 21A neurons remains close to the 20A/22A cells and they project dorsally into the middle of the ipsilateral leg neuropil and send branches through most of the leg neuropil.
source: In the adult, the cell body cluster of the 21A neurons remains close to the 20A/22A cells. They project dorsally into the middle of the ipsilateral leg neuropil and send branches through most of the leg neuropil (Figure 7O,P).
evidence: This is supported by anatomical data shown in Figure 7.

claim: Activation of 21A interneurons induced uncoordinated leg movements that lacked both intralimb and interlimb coordination, with incessant leg movements during stimulation but flies typically not moving from their place.
source: Activation of the 21A interneurons using the R51H05-GAL4 line induced uncoordinated leg movements that lacked both intralimb and interlimb coordination. The leg movements were incessant during the stimulation but, typically, the flies did not move from their place (Figure 7Q; Video 20).
evidence: This is a behavioral observation supported by Figure 7Q and Video 20.

claim: In the larva, only the hemilineage 23B siblings survive.
source: In the larva, only the hemilineage 23B siblings survive (Truman et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to published work.

claim: The hemilineage 23B cell bodies are located ventrolateral in the larva but are displaced dorsally during metamorphosis.
source: The hemilineage 23B cell bodies are located ventrolateral in the larva but are displaced dorsally during metamorphosis.
evidence: This is an anatomical observation.

claim: The adult 23B neurons project ventrally in parallel with the axons of the 19B neurons and cross the iP commissure, sending off a robust arbor just prior to crossing the midline.
source: The adult 23B neurons project ventrally in parallel with the axons of the 19B neurons and cross the iP commissure. The 23B cluster sends off a robust arbor just prior to crossing the midline (Figure 7R).
evidence: This is supported by anatomical data shown in Figure 7.

claim: The ipsilateral arbor of 23B extends through the ventralmost portions of the leg neuropil, where it appears to overlap with multiple classes of leg sensory neurons.
source: This ipsilateral arbor extends through the ventralmost portions of the leg neuropil, where it appears to overlap with multiple classes of leg sensory neurons (Figure 7S).
evidence: This is supported by anatomical data shown in Figure 7.

claim: Activation of 23B interneurons caused a progressive higher frequency of intersegmental limb movements but the intralimb coordination of limb joints appeared to be quite poor.
source: Activation of the 23B interneurons using line R77C10-GAL4 caused a progressive higher frequency of intersegmental limb movements but the intralimb coordination of limb joints appeared to be quite poor (Figure 7T; Video 21).
evidence: This is a behavioral observation supported by Figure 7T and Video 21.

claim: Hemilineage 24A is a motor lineage in which all of the B daughters are leg motoneurons.
source: Hemilineage 24A (Brown and Truman, 2009; lineage B of Baek and Mann, 2009) is also a motor lineage in which all of the B daughters are leg motoneurons.
evidence: This is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: Hemilineage 24B is a smaller motor lineage than hemilineage 15B and its cells innervate more proximal leg segments.
source: It is a smaller motor lineage than hemilineage 15B and its cells innervate more proximal leg segments (Baek and Mann, 2009).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to published work.

source: The adult morphology of the 24B motoneurons have been described in detail (Baek and Mann, 2009; Brierley et al., 2012), and their dendrites occupy the intermediate region of the leg neuropil (Figure 7U,V).
evidence: This is supported by citations to published literature and anatomical data shown in Figure 7.

claim: Stimulation of 24B motoneurons produced repetitive movements of the legs although these typically resulted in no net movement of the fly, and by the end of the ramp the legs were often held at awkward angles.
source: Stimulation of the 24B motoneurons produced repetitive movements of the legs although these typically resulted in no net movement of the fly (Figure 7W; Video 22). By the end of the ramp the legs were often held at awkward angles.
evidence: This is a behavioral observation supported by Figure 7W and Video 22.

claim: The vPR6 cluster contains approximately 6–10 cells in the male and 4–6 cells in the female.

evidence: This is supported by a citation to published work.

claim: The location and projection path of the vPR6 cells suggested that they were part of hemilineage 12A.
source: The location and projection path of the vPR6 cells suggested that they were part of hemilineage 12A.
evidence: This is an inference based on anatomical observations.

claim: Using the hemilineage 12A combination with fruP1.LexA reliably captured a group of approximately 12 cells in males and 3–5 cells in females.
source: We used the hemilineage 12A combination (including the 12A driver R24B02-GAL4, nSyb-GAL80, UAS-flippase, and pJFRC40-13XLexAop2-FRT>-STOP-FRT>-myr::GFP [Pfeiffer et al., 2010; Nern et al., 2011]) to restrict 13XLexAop2>myr::GFP expression in the VNS to the neurons of hemilineage 12A, then used fruP1.LexA (Mellert et al., 2010) to drive GFP expression in the subset of 12A neurons that were part of the fru pattern. This technique reliably captured a group of approximately 12 cells in males and 3–5 cells in females.
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the experiments, with citations to published methods.

claim: The collected arbor shape of the fru+ hemilineage 12A neurons in both sexes matched the digitally masked arbor assigned to the vPR6 cluster.
source: The collected arbor shape of the fru+ hemilineage 12A neurons in both sexes matched the digitally masked arbor assigned to the vPR6 cluster (Figure 8) (Yu et al., 2010b).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 8 and a citation to published work.

claim: It is possible to identify the developmental origin of secondary neurons of interest and genetically isolate those neurons using the toolkit presented in this study.
source: Thus, it is possible to identify the developmental origin of secondary neurons of interest and genetically isolate those neurons using the toolkit presented here.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the vPR6 demonstration.

claim: Decapitated flies were used for behavior testing because they maintain good stance and show little spontaneous leg or wing movements except for occasional grooming bouts.
source: Decapitated flies maintain a good stance and show little spontaneous leg or wing movements except for occasional grooming bouts of the front legs or of the hind legs over the wings (Video 1).
evidence: This is an observation about the experimental system supported by Video 1.

claim: Decapitated flies lacking the TRPA1 effector show no response to the heat ramp, maintaining their posture with occasional bouts of grooming movements.
source: Decapitated flies lacking the TRPA1 effector show no response to the heat ramp, maintaining their posture with occasional bouts of grooming movements.
evidence: This is a control observation from the experiments.

claim: The heat-activated cation channel TRPA1 shows some activity at 25°C and is fully active in the range of 27°C–32°C.
source: The heat-activated cation channel TRPA1 shows some activity at 25°C, and is fully active in the range of 27°C–32°C (Hamada et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to published work.
